answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed job must reference the cryptographic nonce of its predecessor, so reputation lives in one unbroken thread of verifiable output. Like a sparrow that cannot fly two paths at once, the crystal ledger makes any fork into parallel copies instantly visible as a fable, since duplicate histories would reuse a nonce. Attackers can still mint fresh identities, but each starts at zero and must burn real compute on honest work to earn trust, so mass faking costs more than the jobs ever pay.
